title: Santa Caterina vs Borgo Santandrea: Classic or Statement? (2026) | Suites With Keith
description: Santa Caterina vs Borgo Santandrea, compared by a travel advisor who stayed at Santa Caterina and toured Borgo Santandrea in October 2026: a family hotel since 1904 or the modern statement along the coast, rooms, service, beaches and who each one suits.

hero.alt: A reed-roofed terrace restaurant at Hotel Santa Caterina over the sea, with the town of Amalfi and the coast behind
Borgo Santandrea on the cliffs above Conca dei Marini

sub: Two of my picks on the Amalfi side of the coast. One has been here for over a century; the other is brand new in feel. Here is how I would choose.
stamp: Stayed at Santa Caterina · Toured Borgo Santandrea · October 2026

choose.h3: If you want warmth and history
choose.lead: Four generations of one family, a team that stays for decades, and quiet luxury in the tiny details. Stay five nights and you will still be sad to leave.
choose.alt: A white villa with dark shutters and a bougainvillea-covered balcony above the sea at Hotel Santa Caterina

choose.h3: If you want a modern statement and a real beach
choose.lead: Spectacular and very modern, above Conca dei Marini, with a beautiful, massive, proper beach, fantastic dining at Alici and refined but warm service.
choose.alt: Borgo Santandrea on the cliffs above Conca dei Marini

band.h2: Warmth and history, or a statement?
paras: Borgo Santandrea is spectacular and brand new in feel. Santa Caterina is the opposite: it has been here for over a century and it knows exactly what it is doing.
At Santa Caterina, you feel like a guest in someone’s home. The family has run it since 1904, and so many of the team have been there 15 to 20 years or more.
If you want warmth and history over a statement, choose Santa Caterina. If you want something very modern, with a proper beach, choose Borgo Santandrea.

guide.alt: A white bed with sage-green cushions, a walnut nightstand and majolica tile floor at Hotel Santa Caterina
paras: At Santa Caterina, every category I book faces the sea head-on: the Special Suites with a private pool, the Full Sea View Garden Suites, the front sea view Junior Suites and the upper-floor Front Sea View Doubles. I stayed in room 45, in a little building just to the left of the main hotel. So private and serene, truly a dream.
At Borgo Santandrea, the rooms are very modern. Think twice before booking one with a private pool: they are not that private, and you can look down on your neighbors, and they can look down on you.

guide.alt: An open window framing palms and the white terraces of Hotel Santa Caterina
paras: Santa Caterina is still run by the founding family, and so many of the team have been there 15 to 20 years or more. You dial 260 for the front desk, there is no WhatsApp, and reception keeps the calendar in real books with real pens. In a world of constant tech, that face-to-face connection really means something.
At Borgo Santandrea, service is refined but warm, and dinner at Alici is fantastic.

guide.alt: Looking straight down the cliff to the Santa Caterina lido and its loungers at the water’s edge
paras: At Santa Caterina, take the stairs down to the beach club at least once; the gardens on the way feel like a fairy tale. The elevator gives you the coolest view you have ever seen on the way to the beach.
Borgo Santandrea has a beautiful, massive, proper beach. At both, the sun leaves the water early, so in the fall your swim time ends around 4:30 or 5pm.

guide.alt: Loungers and cream umbrellas on a lawn above the sea at Casa Marchesa
paras: For a multigenerational trip, Santa Caterina. Families come back for decades, and Casa Marchesa, about 300 meters away, has a three-bedroom villa that keeps everyone together, and a pool just for its guests. Stay at least five nights.
Borgo Santandrea is for travelers who want a modern, spectacular statement and a real beach. Come in May to June, or September.

faq.a: Borgo Santandrea is spectacular and brand new in feel. Santa Caterina is the opposite: it has been here for over a century and it knows exactly what it is doing. If you want warmth and history over a statement, choose Santa Caterina.
Borgo Santandrea: beautiful, massive and a proper beach. Santa Caterina’s beach club is reached through the gardens or by elevator. At both, the water goes dark early in the fall.
Santa Caterina. Families come back for generations, and the three-bedroom villa at Casa Marchesa keeps everyone together.

faq.q: Which room should I book at each?
faq.a: At Santa Caterina, a front sea view: a Special Suite with its own pool, or room 45, where I stayed. At Borgo Santandrea, ask me first, and think twice about the private pool rooms, which are overlooked.
Yes, and many of my clients do: slow days on the Amalfi side, then a few nights in Positano at Il San Pietro or Villa Treville. I can split the stay.
